source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον.

records.literal_gloss: After these things having departed from the Athens he came to Corinth.

en.L: After these things, having left Athens, he came to Corinth.
en.B: After this, Paul left Athens and went on to Corinth.
en.R: After this, Paul left the city of Athens and went to the city of Corinth.

es.L: Después de estas cosas, saliendo de Atenas, fue a Corinto.
es.B: Después de esto, Pablo salió de Atenas y siguió hasta Corinto.
es.R: Después de esto, Pablo salió de la ciudad de Atenas y fue a la ciudad de Corinto.

fr.L: Après cela, ayant quitté Athènes, il vint à Corinthe.
fr.B: Après cela, Paul quitta Athènes et se rendit à Corinthe.
fr.R: Ensuite, Paul a quitté la ville d’Athènes et il est allé dans la ville de Corinthe.

sw.L: Baada ya mambo haya, akiisha kuondoka Athene, alifika Korintho.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Paulo aliondoka Athene, akaenda Korintho.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Paulo aliuacha mji wa Athene, akaenda mji wa Korintho.

decisions.choice: Corinth: the leading city of the province of Achaia
decisions.reason: Corinth stood on the narrow neck of land between mainland Greece and the Peloponnese, with a port on each sea (Cenchreae, 18:18, was the eastern one). Rome destroyed the old city in 146 BC, and Julius Caesar refounded it as a Roman colony in 44 BC. It was the seat of the proconsul of Achaia (18:12).

decisions.choice: he: Paul, who had been in Athens (17:16-34)
decisions.reason: Paul was alone in Athens; Silas and Timothy join him later (18:5).

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Paul at the start of a new chapter and a new place.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As for the whole book (1:3): the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Greek imperfects ("il discutait", "ils croyaient") stay imperfects. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν, Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει, προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸ διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης, προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἠργάζετο, ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ τῇ τέχνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And having found a certain Jew by name Aquila, of Pontus by the birth, recently having come from the Italy, and Priscilla wife of him, because of the having commanded Claudius to depart all the Jews from the Rome, he came to them, \v 3 and because of the same trade to be he stayed with them and worked; they were for tentmakers by the trade.

en.L: And having found a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome, he went to them, \v 3 and because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked; for they were tentmakers by trade.
en.B: There he met a Jew called Aquila, born in Pontus, who had lately arrived from Italy with his wife Priscilla, since Claudius had ordered every Jew to leave Rome. Paul went to see them, \v 3 and because he and they worked at the same craft, he stayed in their home and worked with them. By trade they were tentmakers.
en.R: In Corinth Paul met a Jew named Aquila. He came from Pontus, but he and his wife Priscilla had recently come to Corinth from Italy. They left Italy because the emperor Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave the city of Rome. Paul went to visit them. \v 3 They did the same kind of work as Paul: they made tents. So Paul stayed with them and worked with them.

es.L: Y habiendo encontrado a un judío llamado Aquila, natural del Ponto, recién llegado de Italia, y a Priscila su mujer, porque Claudio había ordenado que todos los judíos salieran de Roma, fue a ellos, \v 3 y como era del mismo oficio, se quedó con ellos y trabajaba; porque eran fabricantes de tiendas de oficio.
es.B: Allí conoció a un judío llamado Aquila, nacido en el Ponto, que acababa de llegar de Italia con su esposa Priscila, porque Claudio había ordenado que todos los judíos salieran de Roma. Pablo fue a verlos, \v 3 y como tenían el mismo oficio, se quedó en su casa y trabajaba con ellos. Eran fabricantes de tiendas de campaña.
es.R: En Corinto, Pablo conoció a un judío llamado Aquila. Era del Ponto, pero él y su esposa Priscila habían llegado hacía poco a Corinto desde Italia. Habían salido de Italia porque el emperador Claudio había ordenado a todos los judíos que salieran de la ciudad de Roma. Pablo fue a visitarlos. \v 3 Ellos hacían el mismo trabajo que Pablo: fabricaban tiendas de campaña. Así que Pablo se quedó con ellos y trabajó con ellos.

fr.L: Et ayant trouvé un Juif nommé Aquilas, originaire du Pont, récemment arrivé d’Italie, ainsi que Priscille, sa femme, parce que Claude avait ordonné que tous les Juifs quittent Rome, il alla vers eux, \v 3 et, parce qu’il était du même métier, il logeait chez eux et travaillait ; car ils étaient fabricants de tentes de métier.
fr.B: Il y fit la connaissance d’un Juif nommé Aquilas, né dans le Pont, qui venait d’arriver d’Italie avec sa femme Priscille, parce que Claude avait ordonné à tous les Juifs de quitter Rome. Paul alla les voir \v 3 et, comme il exerçait le même métier qu’eux, il logea chez eux et travailla avec eux. Leur métier était de fabriquer des tentes.
fr.R: À Corinthe, Paul a rencontré un Juif appelé Aquilas. Il venait de la région du Pont, mais lui et sa femme Priscille venaient d’arriver d’Italie à Corinthe. Ils avaient quitté l’Italie parce que l’empereur Claude avait ordonné à tous les Juifs de quitter la ville de Rome. Paul est allé leur rendre visite. \v 3 Ils faisaient le même travail que Paul : ils fabriquaient des tentes. Alors Paul est resté chez eux et il a travaillé avec eux.

sw.L: Na akiisha kumkuta Myahudi mmoja jina lake Akila, mzaliwa wa Ponto, aliyekuwa amekuja karibuni kutoka Italia, pamoja na Prisila mke wake, kwa sababu Klaudio alikuwa ameamuru Wayahudi wote waondoke Roma, alikwenda kwao, \v 3 na kwa kuwa walikuwa na kazi moja, alikaa kwao akafanya kazi; kwa maana kazi yao ilikuwa kushona mahema.
sw.B: Huko alimkuta Myahudi mmoja aitwaye Akila, mzaliwa wa Ponto, ambaye alikuwa amewasili karibuni kutoka Italia pamoja na mke wake Prisila, kwa kuwa Klaudio alikuwa ameamuru kila Myahudi aondoke Roma. Paulo alikwenda kuwaona, \v 3 na kwa sababu yeye na wao walikuwa na ufundi mmoja, alikaa nyumbani kwao, akafanya kazi pamoja nao. Kazi yao ilikuwa kushona mahema.
sw.R: Huko Korintho Paulo alikutana na Myahudi mmoja aitwaye Akila. Akila alitoka Ponto, lakini yeye na mke wake Prisila walikuwa wamefika Korintho karibuni kutoka Italia. Waliondoka Italia kwa sababu mfalme Klaudio alikuwa ameamuru Wayahudi wote waondoke mji wa Roma. Paulo alikwenda kuwatembelea. \v 3 Walifanya kazi ileile kama Paulo: walishona mahema. Kwa hiyo Paulo alikaa kwao, akafanya kazi pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: Claudius's order sending the Jews out of Rome, probably about AD 49
alternatives: a date early in Claudius's reign, AD 41
decisions.reason: Claudius was emperor from AD 41 to 54. The Roman writer Suetonius (Claudius 25.4) says that Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome because they were constantly rioting at the prompting of "Chrestus", a form of the name Christ. The date AD 49 comes from the fifth-century writer Orosius, whose source is not known. Dio Cassius (60.6.6) speaks instead of a ban on Jewish meetings in AD 41, which some connect with the same events. So the year is not certain.

decisions.choice: all the Jews: the order as it was given, not a claim that every Jew left
alternatives: every Jew without exception left Rome
decisions.reason: Luke reports the terms of the order. Jews were living in Rome again a few years later: Priscilla and Aquila themselves were back there when Paul wrote Romans (Romans 16:3), and Paul meets the Jewish leaders of Rome in 28:17.

decisions.choice: Aquila and Priscilla: a Jewish couple from Pontus who had lived in Rome
alternatives: already leaders of the church in Rome
decisions.reason: Pontus was a region on the south coast of the Black Sea. The couple appear again in 18:18, 18:26, Romans 16:3, 1 Corinthians 16:19 and 2 Timothy 4:19, where Paul calls her Prisca, the shorter form of the name. Luke does not say whether they were already believers when Paul met them.

decisions.choice: tentmakers: people who made tents, perhaps leatherworkers more generally
decisions.reason: The word means a maker of tents. Tents were made of leather or of cloth woven from goat hair, so the trade may have been leatherwork of many kinds. The word itself does not settle which material they worked in.

decisions.choice: Paul worked with his hands to support himself
alternatives: he worked only to help the couple
decisions.reason: Paul says he earned his own living so as not to be a burden to the churches (20:34; 1 Corinthians 4:12; 9:6-15; 1 Thessalonians 2:9).

decisions.choice: the Greek order, close to other literal versions
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Greek sentence closely, so it will look like other word-for-word translations here.

decisions.choice: the emperor Claudius
decisions.reason: Readable says who Claudius was.

decisions.choice: Priscila
decisions.reason: Luke uses the longer, familiar form of her name, and Spanish keeps "Priscila" here and in verses 18 and 26; Paul's letters use the short form, "Prisca" (meaning decision m3 names the couple).

decisions.choice: Aquilas, Priscille (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: These are the usual French forms of the two names, as Claude is for Claudius and Gallion for Gallio (18:12).

decisions.choice: Akila, Prisila
decisions.reason: Luke uses the familiar form of her name, so "Prisila" here; Romans 16:3 has the short form "Priska", as Paul writes it. The same in 18:18 and 18:26.

decisions.choice: kushona mahema
decisions.reason: Tents were sewn from leather or cloth (meaning decision), so "kushona mahema" (to sew tents) says what the craft was; a footnote in the English notes that they may have been leatherworkers more generally.

source.text: διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον, ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας.

records.literal_gloss: He was reasoning now in the synagogue on every Sabbath, persuading both Jews and Greeks.

en.L: And he was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath and was persuading both Jews and Greeks.
en.B: Each Sabbath he debated in the synagogue, seeking to win over Jews and Greeks alike.
en.R: Every Sabbath day Paul went to the synagogue. He talked with the people there and tried to convince both Jews and Greeks to believe the message about Jesus.

es.L: Y discutía en la sinagoga cada sábado, y persuadía a judíos y a griegos.
es.B: Cada sábado debatía en la sinagoga, tratando de convencer tanto a judíos como a griegos.
es.R: Cada sábado Pablo iba a la sinagoga. Hablaba con la gente de allí y trataba de convencer a judíos y a griegos de que creyeran el mensaje acerca de Jesús.

fr.L: Et il discutait dans la synagogue chaque sabbat, et il persuadait Juifs et Grecs.
fr.B: Chaque sabbat, il discutait dans la synagogue, cherchant à convaincre Juifs et Grecs.
fr.R: Chaque jour de sabbat, Paul allait à la synagogue. Il parlait avec les gens qui étaient là et il essayait de convaincre les Juifs et les Grecs de croire au message sur Jésus.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akihojiana [nao] katika sinagogi kila Sabato, akiwashawishi Wayahudi na Wagiriki.
sw.B: Kila Sabato alijadiliana nao katika sinagogi, akijaribu kuwavuta Wayahudi na Wagiriki pia.
sw.R: Kila siku ya Sabato Paulo alikwenda katika sinagogi. Alizungumza na watu wa huko, akajaribu kuwashawishi Wayahudi na Wagiriki wauamini ujumbe kuhusu Yesu.

decisions.choice: reasoning: discussing and arguing, from the Scriptures
alternatives: giving a speech with no exchange
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Paul's dialogues in the synagogues (17:2, 17:17, 18:19, 19:8). In 17:2-3 he reasons from the Scriptures that the Messiah had to suffer and rise.

decisions.choice: was persuading: he kept trying to persuade
decisions.reason: The tense describes an action that went on. It can mean either that he tried to persuade or that he won people over; 18:8 shows that some did believe.

decisions.choice: Greeks: Gentiles who attended the synagogue
decisions.reason: Gentiles who worshiped Israel's God often came to synagogues (13:16, 13:26, 17:4). Titius Justus in 18:7 is one of them.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: no addition
alternatives: Codex Bezae adds that he put in the name of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and some other witnesses of the Western text expand the verse, saying that Paul inserted the name of the Lord Jesus as he spoke. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: to believe the message about Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul wanted them to be persuaded of, as 18:5 states.

source.text: Ὡς δὲ κατῆλθον ἀπὸ τῆς Μακεδονίας ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος, συνείχετο τῷ λόγῳ ὁ Παῦλος, διαμαρτυρόμενος τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις εἶναι τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: When now came down from the Macedonia both Silas and the Timothy, was being occupied with the word the Paul, earnestly testifying to the Jews to be the Christ Jesus.

en.L: And when both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was wholly occupied with the word, solemnly testifying to the Jews that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was Jesus.
en.B: Once Silas and Timothy had come down from Macedonia, Paul gave himself fully to the word, bearing witness to the Jews that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.R: Later Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia to join Paul. After that, Paul spent all his time telling people God's message. He told the Jews clearly that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the one God had promised to send.

es.L: Y cuando Silas y Timoteo descendieron de Macedonia, Pablo se dedicaba por entero a la palabra, testificando solemnemente a los judíos que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} era Jesús.
es.B: Cuando Silas y Timoteo llegaron de Macedonia, Pablo se entregó por completo a la palabra, dando testimonio a los judíos de que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.R: Más tarde, Silas y Timoteo llegaron de Macedonia para unirse a Pablo. Desde entonces, Pablo dedicó todo su tiempo a anunciar el mensaje de Dios. Les dijo claramente a los judíos que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el que Dios había prometido enviar.

fr.L: Et quand Silas et Timothée furent descendus de Macédoine, Paul était tout occupé par la parole, attestant aux Juifs que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} était Jésus.
fr.B: Une fois Silas et Timothée descendus de Macédoine, Paul se consacra entièrement à la parole, attestant aux Juifs que Jésus était le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Plus tard, Silas et Timothée sont venus de Macédoine pour rejoindre Paul. Après cela, Paul a passé tout son temps à annoncer le message de Dieu. Il a dit clairement aux Juifs que Jésus est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, celui que Dieu avait promis d’envoyer.

sw.L: Na Sila na Timotheo waliposhuka kutoka Makedonia, Paulo alikuwa amejitoa kabisa kwa neno, akiwashuhudia Wayahudi kwa bidii kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni Yesu.
sw.B: Sila na Timotheo walipofika kutoka Makedonia, Paulo alijitoa kikamilifu kwa kazi ya kuhubiri neno, akiwashuhudia Wayahudi kwamba Yesu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Baadaye Sila na Timotheo walikuja kutoka Makedonia kujiunga na Paulo. Tangu hapo Paulo alitumia muda wake wote kuwaambia watu ujumbe wa Mungu. Aliwaeleza Wayahudi waziwazi kwamba Yesu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, yule ambaye Mungu aliahidi kumtuma.

decisions.choice: Silas and Timothy rejoin Paul
alternatives: they meet him for the first time
decisions.reason: Paul had left them in Berea (17:14-15) and asked them to come to him quickly. 1 Thessalonians 3:6 says Timothy brought Paul good news from Thessalonica; Paul wrote that letter with Silvanus (Silas) and Timothy (1 Thessalonians 1:1).

decisions.choice: was wholly occupied with the word: he gave all his time to preaching
alternatives: he was pressed hard by the message
he was distressed about the message
decisions.reason: The verb means to be held fast or absorbed by something. Here it is likely that Paul could now stop his tentmaking for a time, perhaps because the friends from Macedonia brought gifts (2 Corinthians 11:9; Philippians 4:15).

decisions.choice: the Christ was Jesus: the promised Messiah is this man Jesus
alternatives: Jesus was a Christ, one anointed figure among others
decisions.reason: The word with the article is the subject: the one the Jews were waiting for is Jesus. It is a title here, not a second name. The same words come in 18:28 (compare 9:22, 17:3).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "with the word"
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "in the spirit"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("pressed in the spirit"), have "in the spirit" in place of "with the word". The earliest manuscripts have "the word". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: that Jesus is the Messiah (with Christ as the setting)
decisions.reason: Both orders say the same thing in English. Literal keeps the Greek order; Balanced and Readable use the order English readers expect.

decisions.choice: the one God had promised to send
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title.

source.text: ἀντιτασσομένων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν· καθαρὸς ἐγώ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πορεύσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: Opposing however of them and reviling, having shaken out the garments he said to them, The blood of you upon the head of you; clean I; from the now to the Gentiles I will go.

en.L: But when they opposed and reviled [him], he shook out [his] garments and said to them, "Your blood [be] on your head; I [am] clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
en.B: But they set themselves against him and spoke abusively, so he shook out his clothes and said to them, "Your blood is on your own heads. I am clear of it. From now on I am going to the Gentiles."
en.R: But the Jews there argued against Paul and said insulting things. So Paul shook out his clothes, to show that he was no longer responsible for them. He said, "If God punishes you, the blame is yours, not mine. I have done what I should. From now on I will go to the Gentiles, the people who are not Jews."

es.L: Pero como ellos se oponían y [lo] insultaban, sacudiendo [sus] vestidos les dijo: «{{plural_you:La sangre de ustedes|Vuestra sangre}} [sea] sobre {{plural_you:la cabeza de ustedes|vuestra cabeza}}; yo [estoy] limpio. Desde ahora iré a los gentiles».
es.B: Pero ellos se le opusieron y lo insultaban, así que sacudió su ropa y les dijo: «{{plural_you:La sangre de ustedes|Vuestra sangre}} está sobre {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} propias cabezas. Yo quedo libre de culpa. De ahora en adelante iré a los gentiles».
es.R: Pero los judíos de allí discutían contra Pablo y decían cosas ofensivas. Entonces Pablo sacudió su ropa, para mostrar que ya no era responsable de ellos. Les dijo: «Si Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} castiga, la culpa es {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestra}}, no mía. Yo he hecho lo que debía. De ahora en adelante iré a los gentiles, a la gente que no es judía».

fr.L: Mais comme ils s’opposaient et blasphémaient, il secoua [ses] vêtements et leur dit : « Votre sang [soit] sur votre tête ; moi, [je suis] pur. Dès maintenant, j’irai vers les nations. »
fr.B: Mais comme ils s’opposaient à lui et l’injuriaient, il secoua ses vêtements et leur dit : « Votre sang est sur vos propres têtes. Moi, j’en suis innocent. Désormais, j’irai vers les non-Juifs. »
fr.R: Mais les Juifs de là-bas se sont opposés à Paul et lui ont dit des insultes. Alors Paul a secoué ses vêtements, pour montrer qu’il n’était plus responsable d’eux. Il leur a dit : « Si Dieu vous punit, ce sera votre faute, pas la mienne. J’ai fait ce que je devais faire. À partir de maintenant, j’irai vers les non-Juifs. »

sw.L: Lakini walipompinga na kumtukana, aliyakung'uta mavazi [yake], akawaambia, "Damu yenu [na iwe] juu ya vichwa vyenu; mimi [ni] safi. Tangu sasa nitakwenda kwa watu wa mataifa."
sw.B: Lakini walimpinga na kumtukana. Basi akayakung'uta mavazi yake, akawaambia, "Damu yenu iko juu ya vichwa vyenu wenyewe. Mimi sina hatia. Tangu sasa nakwenda kwa watu wa mataifa."
sw.R: Lakini Wayahudi wa huko walibishana na Paulo, wakamtukana. Kwa hiyo Paulo aliyakung'uta mavazi yake, kuonyesha kwamba hahusiki tena nao. Akasema, "Mungu akiwaadhibu, lawama ni yenu, si yangu. Nimefanya yale niliyopaswa kufanya. Tangu sasa nitakwenda kwa watu wa mataifa, yaani watu wasio Wayahudi."

decisions.choice: reviling: speaking abusively, of Paul and of the Jesus he preached
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak insults. Against people it is abuse; against God or Jesus it is blasphemy. Paul's message was about Jesus, so the insults probably touched both.

decisions.choice: shaking out his garments: a sign that he was done with them and not to blame
alternatives: brushing off dust after a journey
decisions.reason: A public gesture of breaking off. Nehemiah shook out his garment as a sign that God would shake out anyone who broke the oath (Nehemiah 5:13). Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet at Pisidian Antioch (13:51), as Jesus had told his disciples to do (Luke 9:5).

decisions.choice: your blood on your head: you are responsible for your own fate, and I am free of blame
alternatives: a curse that they would die
decisions.reason: The words echo Ezekiel 33:4-9: a watchman who warns the people is free of guilt for those who do not listen. Compare 2 Samuel 1:16 and 20:26, where Paul says he is "clean from the blood" of all.

decisions.choice: to the Gentiles: here in Corinth he turns to the Gentiles
alternatives: he will never again preach to Jews
decisions.reason: Paul says the same in 13:46 and 28:28. In the next city he again goes first to the synagogue (18:19), so this is about the Jews of Corinth, not the Jews everywhere.

decisions.choice: to show that he was no longer responsible for them; If God punishes you, the blame is yours, not mine
alternatives: he shook out his clothes; your blood be on your head
decisions.reason: Readable explains the gesture and the saying, following the meaning notes.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles, the people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Gentiles.

decisions.choice: insultaban
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for blasphemy, but here the abuse is aimed at Paul, and perhaps through him at the Jesus he preached (meaning decision m1). Spanish "blasfemar" would say only that they spoke against God, so Spanish says "insultar", as the English says "reviled".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:La sangre de ustedes|Vuestra sangre}}
decisions.reason: With ustedes, "su sangre" could be read as "his blood", so the span spells out "de ustedes". Every plural "you" in this chapter is the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B, R), without the English Readable's added explanation
alternatives: les non-Juifs, ceux qui ne sont pas juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the New Testament. The English Readable explains "Gentiles"; French "les non-Juifs" already says who they are, so Readable needs no gloss.

source.text: καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἰκίαν τινὸς ὀνόματι Τιτίου Ἰούστου σεβομένου τὸν θεόν, οὗ ἡ οἰκία ἦν συνομοροῦσα τῇ συναγωγῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And having departed from there he went into [the] house of a certain [one] by name Titius Justus, worshiping the God, of whom the house was adjoining the synagogue.

en.L: And departing from there, he went into the house of a certain [man] named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.
en.B: Paul left them and went over to the home of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God. His house stood right beside the synagogue.
en.R: Paul left the synagogue and went to the house of a man named Titius Justus. Titius Justus was not a Jew, but he worshiped God. His house was next to the synagogue.

es.L: Y saliendo de allí, entró en casa de uno llamado Ticio Justo, que adoraba a Dios, cuya casa estaba junto a la sinagoga.
es.B: Pablo los dejó y se fue a la casa de un hombre llamado Ticio Justo, que adoraba a Dios. Su casa estaba justo al lado de la sinagoga.
es.R: Pablo salió de la sinagoga y fue a la casa de un hombre llamado Ticio Justo. Ticio Justo no era judío, pero adoraba a Dios. Su casa estaba al lado de la sinagoga.

fr.L: Et, étant parti de là, il entra dans la maison d’un [homme] nommé Titius Justus, qui adorait Dieu, dont la maison était contiguë à la synagogue.
fr.B: Paul les quitta et se rendit chez un homme nommé Titius Justus, qui adorait Dieu. Sa maison était juste à côté de la synagogue.
fr.R: Paul a quitté la synagogue et il est allé dans la maison d’un homme appelé Titius Justus. Titius Justus n’était pas juif, mais il adorait Dieu. Sa maison était à côté de la synagogue.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuhama kutoka huko, aliingia katika nyumba ya [mtu] mmoja jina lake Titio Yusto, mwabudu wa Mungu, ambaye nyumba yake ilikuwa jirani na sinagogi.
sw.B: Paulo aliwaacha, akahamia nyumbani kwa mtu mmoja aitwaye Titio Yusto, aliyemwabudu Mungu. Nyumba yake ilikuwa karibu kabisa na sinagogi.
sw.R: Paulo aliondoka sinagogini, akaenda nyumbani kwa mtu mmoja aitwaye Titio Yusto. Titio Yusto hakuwa Myahudi, lakini alimwabudu Mungu. Nyumba yake ilikuwa jirani na sinagogi.

decisions.choice: he went into the house: he began to teach there, not in the synagogue
alternatives: he moved his lodging from Aquila and Priscilla to Titius Justus
decisions.reason: "From there" points back to the synagogue of 18:4-6. The house became the place where Paul taught. Luke does not say that Paul stopped living with Aquila and Priscilla.

decisions.choice: a worshiper of God: a Gentile who worshiped Israel's God without becoming a Jew
decisions.reason: Luke uses this phrase for Gentiles who attended the synagogue, such as Lydia (16:14) and the Greeks in 17:4. Titius Justus is a Roman name.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "Titius Justus"
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ over the name. Some have "Titus Justus", and many later ones, followed by the King James Version, have "Justus" alone. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Titius Justus was not a Jew, but he worshiped God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase meant for a Gentile, following the meaning note. Luke does not say outright that he was a Gentile.

decisions.choice: Titio Yusto
decisions.reason: The Latin names in Swahili form, "Yusto" as in 1:23; "Titio" is kept apart from Titus ("Tito"), a different man.

source.text: Κρίσπος δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἐπίστευσεν τῷ κυρίῳ σὺν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν Κορινθίων ἀκούοντες ἐπίστευον καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο.

records.literal_gloss: Crispus now the synagogue ruler believed in the Lord with whole the household of him, and many of the Corinthians hearing were believing and were being baptized.

en.L: And Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with his whole household, and many of the Corinthians, hearing, believed and were baptized.
en.B: Crispus, who led the synagogue, believed in the Lord, and so did everyone in his household. Many other people in Corinth heard the message, believed and were baptized.
en.R: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his house believed in the Lord. Many other people in Corinth heard the message about Jesus. They believed in Jesus and were baptized.

es.L: Y Crispo, el jefe de la sinagoga, creyó en el Señor con toda su casa, y muchos de los corintios, al oír, creían y eran bautizados.
es.B: Crispo, el jefe de la sinagoga, creyó en el Señor, y también todos los de su casa. Muchos otros corintios oyeron el mensaje, creyeron y fueron bautizados.
es.R: Crispo era el jefe de la sinagoga. Él y todos los de su casa creyeron en el Señor. Muchas otras personas de Corinto oyeron el mensaje acerca de Jesús. Creyeron en Jesús y fueron bautizados.

fr.L: Et Crispus, le chef de la synagogue, crut au Seigneur avec toute sa maison, et beaucoup de Corinthiens, en entendant, croyaient et étaient baptisés.
fr.B: Crispus, qui dirigeait la synagogue, crut au Seigneur, ainsi que toute sa maisonnée. Beaucoup d’autres habitants de Corinthe entendirent le message, crurent et furent baptisés.
fr.R: Crispus était le chef de la synagogue. Lui et tous ceux de sa maison ont cru au Seigneur. Beaucoup d’autres personnes à Corinthe ont entendu le message sur Jésus. Elles ont cru en Jésus et elles ont été baptisées.

sw.L: Na Krispo, mkuu wa sinagogi, alimwamini Bwana pamoja na nyumba yake yote, na wengi wa Wakorintho, waliposikia, waliamini na kubatizwa.
sw.B: Krispo, kiongozi wa sinagogi, alimwamini Bwana, na vivyo hivyo watu wote wa nyumbani mwake. Wakorintho wengine wengi walisikia ujumbe, wakaamini, wakabatizwa.
sw.R: Krispo alikuwa kiongozi wa sinagogi. Yeye na watu wote wa nyumbani mwake walimwamini Bwana. Watu wengine wengi wa Korintho walisikia ujumbe kuhusu Yesu. Wakamwamini Yesu, wakabatizwa.

decisions.choice: Crispus, the synagogue ruler: the official who arranged the synagogue's meetings
decisions.reason: The ruler of a synagogue chose who would read and speak (13:15; Luke 8:41). Paul says he baptized Crispus himself (1 Corinthians 1:14). His coming to faith was a striking event after 18:6.

decisions.choice: his whole household: his family and everyone who lived in his house
decisions.reason: A household included family members, slaves and others who lived there, as with Cornelius (10:2, 11:14) and the jailer at Philippi (16:31-34).

decisions.choice: were believing and were being baptized: one after another, over a period of time
decisions.reason: The tenses describe something that kept happening during Paul's stay (18:11).

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul's message was about Jesus (18:5), and "believed in the Lord" in Acts usually means believing in Jesus (9:42, 11:17, 16:31).

decisions.choice: heard the message (B); heard the message about Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was heard.

decisions.choice: el jefe de la sinagoga
decisions.reason: The term used for the synagogue leader across the Spanish New Testament: the official who arranged the meetings (meaning decision m1), not a rabbi. The same for Sosthenes in verse 17.

decisions.choice: mkuu wa sinagogi (L); kiongozi wa sinagogi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the project's Swahili term list and 13:15 have it; the same for Sosthenes in 18:17.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος ἐν νυκτὶ δι’ ὁράματος τῷ Παύλῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, ἀλλὰ λάλει καὶ μὴ σιωπήσῃς, διότι ἐγώ εἰμι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε, διότι λαός ἐστί μοι πολὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Said now the Lord in night through a vision to the Paul, Not fear, but speak and not be silent, \v 10 because I am with you and no one will set upon you to harm you, because people is to me much in the city this.

en.L: And the Lord said to Paul in [the] night through a vision, "Do not fear, but speak and do not be silent, \v 10 because I am with you, and no one will set upon you to harm you, because there are many people [belonging] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this city."
en.B: In a vision at night the Lord told Paul, "Stop being afraid. Go on speaking, and do not fall silent. \v 10 I am with you. No one will lay a hand on you to hurt you, because many in this city belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: One night Paul saw a vision. In it the Lord said to him, "Do not be afraid. Keep telling people about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not stop. \v 10 I am with you. No one will attack you or hurt you. There are many people in this city who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Y el Señor dijo a Pablo de noche por medio de una visión: «No temas, sino habla y no calles, \v 10 porque yo estoy contigo, y nadie te atacará para hacerte daño, porque hay mucho pueblo [que es] {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} en esta ciudad».
es.B: Una noche, en una visión, el Señor le dijo a Pablo: «Deja de tener miedo. Sigue hablando y no te calles. \v 10 Yo estoy contigo. Nadie te pondrá la mano encima para hacerte daño, porque muchos en esta ciudad son {{deity_pronoun:míos|Míos}}».
es.R: Una noche Pablo tuvo una visión. En ella el Señor le dijo: «No tengas miedo. Sigue hablándole a la gente acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y no te detengas. \v 10 Yo estoy contigo. Nadie te atacará ni te hará daño. En esta ciudad hay mucha gente que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece».

fr.L: Et le Seigneur dit à Paul, de nuit, par une vision : « Ne crains pas, mais parle et ne te tais pas, \v 10 parce que je suis avec toi, et personne ne se jettera sur toi pour te faire du mal, parce qu’il y a un peuple nombreux [qui est] à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans cette ville. »
fr.B: Dans une vision, de nuit, le Seigneur dit à Paul : « Cesse d’avoir peur. Continue de parler, et ne te tais pas. \v 10 Je suis avec toi. Personne ne portera la main sur toi pour te faire du mal, car, dans cette ville, beaucoup {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiennent. »
fr.R: Une nuit, Paul a eu une vision. Le Seigneur lui a dit : « N’aie pas peur. Continue à parler de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aux gens, et ne t’arrête pas. \v 10 Je suis avec toi. Personne ne va t’attaquer ni te faire du mal. Dans cette ville, il y a beaucoup de gens qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiennent. »

sw.L: Na Bwana alimwambia Paulo usiku katika maono, "Usiogope, bali nena wala usinyamaze, \v 10 kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko pamoja nawe, na hakuna mtu atakayekushambulia ili akudhuru, kwa sababu ninao watu wengi katika mji huu."
sw.B: Usiku mmoja Bwana alimwambia Paulo katika maono, "Acha kuogopa. Endelea kuhubiri, wala usinyamaze. \v 10 Mimi niko pamoja nawe. Hakuna mtu atakayekushambulia ili akudhuru, kwa sababu katika mji huu kuna watu wengi walio {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.R: Usiku mmoja Paulo aliona maono. Ndani ya maono hayo Bwana alimwambia, "Usiogope. Endelea kuwaambia watu habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, wala usiache. \v 10 Mimi niko pamoja nawe. Hakuna mtu atakayekushambulia wala kukuumiza. Kuna watu wengi katika mji huu walio {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: the Lord: the risen Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul sees and hears the risen Jesus in other visions (9:4-6, 22:17-21, 23:11). In 23:11 the Lord who stands by him at night tells him to take heart, as here.

decisions.choice: stop being afraid; keep on speaking
alternatives: do not start to be afraid
decisions.reason: The commands are in the present tense, which suits going on with something or stopping something already under way. Paul was speaking under threat (18:6), and 1 Corinthians 2:3 says he was with them "in weakness and in fear and in much trembling".

decisions.choice: I am with you: the promise God gives to those he sends
decisions.reason: God says these words to Jacob (Genesis 28:15), to Joshua (Joshua 1:5, 1:9) and to Jeremiah, adding "do not be afraid" (Jeremiah 1:8; compare Isaiah 41:10). Jesus promised the same to his disciples (Matthew 28:20).

decisions.choice: set upon you to harm you: attack you so as to do you harm
decisions.reason: Paul is still accused (18:12), but no one is able to hurt him.

decisions.choice: many people belonging to me: many in Corinth whom the Lord will bring to faith
decisions.reason: The word for people is the one used for Israel as God's people. In 15:14 James says God has taken from the Gentiles "a people for his name". Here the Lord counts as his own many in Corinth who have not yet believed.

decisions.choice: keep telling people about me
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul was to speak about.

decisions.choice: ninao (L); walio {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The risen Lord speaks (meaning decision). At Literal "to me" is inside the verb "ninao" (I have), which cannot take a capital, so the English "me" span has no Literal counterpart; Balanced and Readable span the possessive "wangu". "Mimi" opens its sentence and is written plainly.

source.text: ἐκάθισεν δὲ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ μῆνας ἓξ διδάσκων ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He sat now a year and months six teaching among them the word of the God.

en.L: And he stayed a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
en.B: Paul stayed on for eighteen months, teaching the word of God among them.
en.R: Paul stayed in Corinth for a year and a half. He taught the people there the word of God.

es.L: Y se quedó un año y seis meses, enseñando entre ellos la palabra de Dios.
es.B: Pablo se quedó allí dieciocho meses, enseñando entre ellos la palabra de Dios.
es.R: Pablo se quedó en Corinto un año y medio. Enseñó a la gente de allí la palabra de Dios.

fr.L: Et il resta un an et six mois, enseignant parmi eux la parole de Dieu.
fr.B: Paul resta dix-huit mois à enseigner parmi eux la parole de Dieu.
fr.R: Paul est resté à Corinthe pendant un an et demi. Il a enseigné la parole de Dieu aux gens de la ville.

sw.L: Naye akakaa mwaka mmoja na miezi sita, akifundisha neno la Mungu kati yao.
sw.B: Paulo alikaa huko kwa mwaka mmoja na nusu, akilifundisha neno la Mungu kati yao.
sw.R: Paulo alikaa Korintho kwa mwaka mmoja na nusu. Aliwafundisha watu wa huko neno la Mungu.

decisions.choice: sat: stayed, settled
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to sit or to settle in a place. Here it says how long Paul stayed.

decisions.choice: a year and six months: perhaps the length of the whole stay, or the time before the events of 18:12
decisions.reason: After the hearing before Gallio, Paul stays "many days more" (18:18). It is not clear whether those days are counted in the eighteen months.

source.text: Γαλλίωνος δὲ ἀνθυπάτου ὄντος τῆς Ἀχαΐας κατεπέστησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα, λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ τὸν νόμον ἀναπείθει οὗτος τοὺς ἀνθρώπους σέβεσθαι τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: Gallio however proconsul being of the Achaia, rose up with one accord the Jews against the Paul and led him to the judgment seat, \v 13 saying that, Contrary to the law persuades this [one] the men to worship the God.

en.L: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and led him to the judgment seat, \v 13 saying, "This [man] persuades {{gender:people|men}} to worship God contrary to the law."
en.B: But while Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews joined forces against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat. \v 13 Their charge was this: "He is talking people into worshiping God in a way the law does not allow."
en.R: Later, Gallio became proconsul, the Roman governor of Achaia. Then the Jews all joined together against Paul and took him to court in front of Gallio. \v 13 They said, "This man is teaching people to worship God in a way that breaks the law."

es.L: Pero siendo Galión procónsul de Acaya, los judíos se levantaron de común acuerdo contra Pablo y lo llevaron al tribunal, \v 13 diciendo: «Este persuade a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} a adorar a Dios contra la ley».
es.B: Pero cuando Galión era procónsul de Acaya, los judíos se pusieron de acuerdo contra Pablo y lo llevaron ante el tribunal. \v 13 Esta fue su acusación: «Este hombre convence a la gente de que adore a Dios de una manera que la ley no permite».
es.R: Más tarde, Galión llegó a ser procónsul, es decir, el gobernador romano de Acaya. Entonces todos los judíos se unieron contra Pablo y lo llevaron ante el tribunal, delante de Galión. \v 13 Dijeron: «Este hombre está enseñando a la gente a adorar a Dios de una manera que va contra la ley».

fr.L: Mais, Gallion étant proconsul de l’Achaïe, les Juifs se dressèrent d’un commun accord contre Paul et le menèrent au tribunal, \v 13 en disant : « C’est contrairement à la loi que celui-ci persuade {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} d’adorer Dieu. »
fr.B: Mais, alors que Gallion était proconsul d’Achaïe, les Juifs s’unirent contre Paul et l’amenèrent devant le tribunal. \v 13 Voici leur accusation : « Cet homme pousse les gens à adorer Dieu d’une manière que la loi n’autorise pas. »
fr.R: Plus tard, Gallion est devenu proconsul, c’est-à-dire le gouverneur romain de l’Achaïe. Alors les Juifs se sont tous unis contre Paul et l’ont emmené au tribunal, devant Gallion. \v 13 Ils ont dit : « Cet homme enseigne aux gens à adorer Dieu d’une manière qui va contre la loi. »

sw.L: Lakini Galio alipokuwa mkuu wa jimbo la Akaya, Wayahudi kwa nia moja walimwinukia Paulo, wakampeleka mbele ya kiti cha hukumu, \v 13 wakisema, "Huyu anawashawishi watu wamwabudu Mungu kinyume cha sheria."
sw.B: Lakini wakati Galio alipokuwa mkuu wa jimbo la Akaya, Wayahudi waliungana dhidi ya Paulo, wakamleta mbele ya kiti cha hukumu. \v 13 Wakamshtaki hivi: "Mtu huyu anawavuta watu wamwabudu Mungu kwa namna ambayo sheria hairuhusu."
sw.R: Baadaye Galio alikuwa mkuu wa jimbo, yaani mtawala wa Kirumi wa Akaya. Ndipo Wayahudi wote waliungana dhidi ya Paulo, wakampeleka mahakamani mbele ya Galio. \v 13 Wakasema, "Mtu huyu anawafundisha watu wamwabudu Mungu kwa namna inayovunja sheria."

decisions.choice: Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, about AD 51-52
decisions.reason: Gallio was the brother of the philosopher Seneca. A letter of the emperor Claudius carved in stone at Delphi (the Gallio inscription) names him as proconsul. It dates his year in office to about AD 51-52, which helps date Paul's stay in Corinth. A proconsul governed a senatorial province such as Achaia, usually for one year.

decisions.choice: when Gallio was proconsul: perhaps soon after he arrived
alternatives: at the end of his term
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the time. A new governor was a natural moment for the Jews to try their case again, but Luke does not say so.

decisions.choice: the judgment seat: the raised platform where the governor heard cases
decisions.reason: The word means a raised step or platform. Roman officials sat on it in a public place to give judgment (25:6, 25:10, 25:17; Matthew 27:19).

decisions.choice: the law: Jewish law, or Roman law
decisions.reason: The accusers may have meant that Paul's teaching broke Roman law, which allowed Judaism but not new cults. Gallio takes it as a matter of the Jews' own law (18:15). The word alone does not say which law is meant.

decisions.choice: men: people, men and women
decisions.reason: The charge is about anyone Paul persuades, and women were among the believers (17:4, 17:12, 18:2).

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The word means people here; Literal has a gender span.

decisions.choice: proconsul, the Roman governor; took him to court in front of Gallio
alternatives: proconsul; led him to the judgment seat
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title and what the judgment seat was.

decisions.choice: el tribunal
decisions.reason: The judgment seat was the raised platform where the governor heard cases (meaning decision m3); Spanish "tribunal" names both the platform and the court, so it serves at every level, where the English Readable says "court". The same in verses 16 and 17.

decisions.choice: le tribunal at every level
decisions.reason: French "tribunal" names both the governor's raised seat (m3) and the court that sits there, so one word serves every level; the English Readable's change to "court" is not needed. The same in 18:16-17.

decisions.choice: la loi, lowercase
decisions.reason: The charge may appeal to Jewish law or to Roman law (m4, uncertain). The capital would decide for the Law of Moses, so the lowercase keeps the question open. In 18:15 Gallio speaks of "your own law", plainly the Jewish Law, and French writes "Loi" there.

decisions.choice: mkuu wa jimbo (L, B); mkuu wa jimbo, yaani mtawala wa Kirumi (R)
decisions.reason: The Roman proconsul, named as Sergius Paulus is in 13:7; Readable explains it as the English Readable does. "Watu" needs no gender span (the English has "people" with "men" as the alternative).

decisions.choice: kiti cha hukumu (L, B); mahakamani (R)
decisions.reason: The raised platform where the governor heard cases (meaning decision), "kiti cha hukumu" as in 12:21 and Romans 14:10; Readable says the court, as the English Readable does. The same in 18:16-17.

source.text: μέλλοντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἀνοίγειν τὸ στόμα εἶπεν ὁ Γαλλίων πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· Εἰ μὲν ἦν ἀδίκημά τι ἢ ῥᾳδιούργημα πονηρόν, ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι, κατὰ λόγον ἂν ἀνεσχόμην ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Being about now the Paul to open the mouth, said the Gallio to the Jews, If indeed it was wrongdoing some or crime wicked, O Jews, according to reason I would have borne with you;

en.L: But when Paul was about to open [his] mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, "If indeed it were some wrongdoing or wicked crime, O Jews, I would reasonably have put up with you;
en.B: Paul was about to speak when Gallio said to the Jews, "If this were some wrong or a serious crime, you Jews, I would have good reason to take up your case.
en.R: Paul was ready to answer, but Gallio spoke first. He said to the Jews, "If this man had done something wrong or had committed a serious crime, I would of course listen to your complaint.

es.L: Y cuando Pablo iba a abrir la boca, Galión dijo a los judíos: «Si fuera algún agravio o algún crimen perverso, oh judíos, con razón {{plural_you:los|os}} habría soportado;
es.B: Pablo estaba a punto de hablar cuando Galión dijo a los judíos: «Si se tratara de algún delito o de un crimen grave, judíos, sería razonable que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} atendiera.
es.R: Pablo estaba listo para responder, pero Galión habló primero. Dijo a los judíos: «Si este hombre hubiera hecho algo malo o hubiera cometido un crimen grave, claro que yo escucharía {{plural_you:la queja de ustedes|vuestra queja}}.

fr.L: Et comme Paul allait ouvrir la bouche, Gallion dit aux Juifs : « S’il s’agissait de quelque injustice ou de quelque méchant forfait, ô Juifs, je vous aurais écoutés comme de raison ;
fr.B: Paul allait prendre la parole quand Gallion dit aux Juifs : « S’il s’agissait d’un délit ou d’un crime grave, Juifs, j’aurais de bonnes raisons de recevoir votre plainte.
fr.R: Paul allait répondre, mais Gallion a parlé avant lui. Il a dit aux Juifs : « Si cet homme avait fait quelque chose de mal ou commis un crime grave, j’écouterais bien sûr votre plainte.

sw.L: Lakini Paulo alipokuwa karibu kufungua kinywa [chake], Galio aliwaambia Wayahudi, "Kama kweli lingekuwa kosa fulani au uhalifu mbaya, enyi Wayahudi, ingekuwa haki kwangu kuwavumilia;
sw.B: Paulo alipokuwa karibu kusema, Galio aliwaambia Wayahudi, "Kama hili lingekuwa kosa fulani au uhalifu mzito, enyi Wayahudi, ningekuwa na sababu nzuri ya kusikiliza shauri lenu.
sw.R: Paulo alikuwa tayari kujibu, lakini Galio alitangulia kusema. Aliwaambia Wayahudi, "Kama mtu huyu angekuwa amefanya kosa fulani au uhalifu mzito, bila shaka ningesikiliza mashtaka yenu.

decisions.choice: to open his mouth: to begin his defense
decisions.reason: A common way of saying someone begins to speak (8:35, 10:34).

decisions.choice: wrongdoing or wicked crime: an offense against the law, or a serious act of fraud or villainy
decisions.reason: The first word means a legal wrong. The second means a reckless or wicked deed. Gallio means matters a Roman court would judge.

decisions.choice: if it were ... I would have: but it is not such a case
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the opposite is true: there is no crime here.

decisions.choice: I would reasonably have put up with you: it would be right for me to hear your case
alternatives: I would have been patient with your manners
decisions.reason: "Put up with" means to hear someone out. "According to reason" means as is fitting or right.

decisions.choice: a full stop, with the quotation still open
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence goes on into 18:15. Balanced and Readable end the English sentence here.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ζητήματά ἐστιν περὶ λόγου καὶ ὀνομάτων καὶ νόμου τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς, ὄψεσθε αὐτοί· κριτὴς ἐγὼ τούτων οὐ βούλομαι εἶναι.

records.literal_gloss: if however questions it is about word and names and law of the according to you, you will see [to it] yourselves; a judge I of these things not wish to be.

en.L: but if it is questions about a word and names and your own law, you will see [to it] yourselves; I do not wish to be a judge of these things."
en.B: But these are disputes over teaching and titles and your own law. Deal with them yourselves. I will not sit in judgment on matters like these."
en.R: But you are arguing about words and names and your own Jewish law. You must settle that yourselves. I will not be a judge of things like that."

es.L: pero si son cuestiones acerca de una palabra y de nombres y de {{plural_you:la ley de ustedes|vuestra ley}}, {{plural_you:ustedes mismos lo verán|vosotros mismos lo veréis}}; yo no quiero ser juez de estas cosas».
es.B: Pero se trata de discusiones sobre enseñanzas y títulos y sobre {{plural_you:la ley de ustedes|vuestra propia ley}}. {{plural_you:Resuélvanlo ustedes mismos|Resolvedlo vosotros mismos}}. Yo no quiero ser juez de semejantes asuntos».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes discuten|vosotros discutís}} sobre palabras y nombres y sobre {{plural_you:la ley judía de ustedes|vuestra propia ley judía}}. {{plural_you:Arréglenlo ustedes mismos|Arregladlo vosotros mismos}}. Yo no voy a juzgar cosas como esas».

fr.L: mais si ce sont des débats au sujet d’une parole, de noms et de votre propre Loi, vous y verrez vous-mêmes ; moi, je ne veux pas être juge de ces choses. »
fr.B: Mais puisqu’il s’agit de discussions sur un enseignement, sur des titres et sur votre propre Loi, réglez cela vous-mêmes. Je refuse de juger de telles affaires. »
fr.R: Mais vous vous disputez à propos de mots, de noms et de votre Loi à vous, la Loi juive. C’est à vous de régler cela. Je ne veux pas juger ce genre d’affaires. »

sw.L: lakini ikiwa ni maswali kuhusu neno na majina na sheria yenu wenyewe, mtaliangalia wenyewe; mimi sitaki kuwa mwamuzi wa mambo haya."
sw.B: Lakini haya ni mabishano juu ya mafundisho na vyeo na sheria yenu wenyewe. Yashughulikieni wenyewe. Mimi sitaketi kuhukumu mambo kama haya."
sw.R: Lakini mnabishana kuhusu maneno na majina na sheria yenu ya Kiyahudi. Ni lazima mlimalize jambo hilo wenyewe. Mimi sitakuwa mwamuzi wa mambo kama hayo."

decisions.choice: but if: but since, as is the case
decisions.reason: After the unreal condition in 18:14, this condition states what Gallio thinks the matter really is.

decisions.choice: a word and names: arguments about teaching and about names or titles
decisions.reason: Gallio speaks with contempt of Jewish disputes. The "names" may be whether Jesus is the Messiah (18:5): the claim was about a name and a title.

decisions.choice: you will see to it yourselves: deal with it yourselves
alternatives: a prediction that they will see
decisions.reason: A future used as a command, as in Matthew 27:4, 27:24.

decisions.choice: Gallio refuses to try the case
alternatives: he finds Paul innocent of a crime
decisions.reason: He treats the dispute as a matter inside Judaism. In practice this left Paul free to go on preaching in Corinth.

decisions.choice: teaching and titles
decisions.reason: Balanced says what kind of words and names were argued over, following the meaning note.

source.text: καὶ ἀπήλασεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος.

records.literal_gloss: And he drove them from the judgment seat.

en.L: And he drove them from the judgment seat.
en.B: Then he had them driven away from the judgment seat.
en.R: Then he made them leave the court.

es.L: Y los echó del tribunal.
es.B: Luego hizo que los expulsaran del tribunal.
es.R: Entonces los hizo salir del tribunal.

fr.L: Et il les chassa du tribunal.
fr.B: Puis il les fit expulser du tribunal.
fr.R: Ensuite, il les a fait sortir du tribunal.

sw.L: Naye akawafukuza kutoka kiti cha hukumu.
sw.B: Kisha akaamuru wafukuzwe mbele ya kiti cha hukumu.
sw.R: Kisha akawafanya waondoke mahakamani.

decisions.choice: drove away: sent them off, probably by his attendants
decisions.reason: The verb means to drive away. A Roman official had attendants who could clear the place.

decisions.choice: the court
decisions.reason: Readable uses a familiar word for the place where the governor judged cases.

source.text: ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος· καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ἔμελεν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seized then all Sosthenes the synagogue ruler they were beating [him] before the judgment seat; and nothing of these things to the Gallio was mattering.

en.L: And they all seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and were beating [him] in front of the judgment seat; and none of these things mattered to Gallio.
en.B: Then they all grabbed Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But Gallio paid no attention to any of it.
en.R: Then they all grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the court. But Gallio did not care at all.

es.L: Y todos, agarrando a Sóstenes, el jefe de la sinagoga, [lo] golpeaban delante del tribunal; y nada de esto le importaba a Galión.
es.B: Entonces todos agarraron a Sóstenes, el jefe de la sinagoga, y lo golpearon delante del tribunal. Pero a Galión nada de esto le preocupaba.
es.R: Entonces todos agarraron a Sóstenes, el jefe de la sinagoga, y le pegaron delante del tribunal. Pero a Galión no le importó en absoluto.

fr.L: Et tous, s’étant saisis de Sosthène, le chef de la synagogue, [le] frappaient devant le tribunal ; et Gallion ne se souciait en rien de cela.
fr.B: Alors tous se saisirent de Sosthène, le chef de la synagogue, et le battirent devant le tribunal. Mais Gallion ne s’en soucia aucunement.
fr.R: Alors ils ont tous attrapé Sosthène, le chef de la synagogue, et ils l’ont battu devant le tribunal. Mais cela n’a pas du tout intéressé Gallion.

sw.L: Ndipo wote wakamkamata Sostene, mkuu wa sinagogi, wakawa wakimpiga mbele ya kiti cha hukumu; na Galio hakujali lolote katika mambo hayo.
sw.B: Kisha wote walimkamata Sostene, kiongozi wa sinagogi, wakampiga mbele ya kiti cha hukumu. Lakini Galio hakujali lolote kati ya hayo.
sw.R: Kisha wote wakamkamata Sostene, kiongozi wa sinagogi, wakampiga mbele ya mahakama. Lakini Galio hakujali hata kidogo.

decisions.choice: all: probably the crowd of onlookers, Gentiles in Corinth
alternatives: the Jews themselves, angry with their own leader
decisions.reason: Luke does not say who "all" were. Gentile onlookers may have taken Gallio's ruling as leave to attack the Jews' leader. It is also possible that the Jews turned on Sosthenes for losing the case.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "all"
alternatives: a few manuscripts read "all the Jews"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "the Greeks", and a few add "the Jews". The earliest manuscripts have only "all". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler: perhaps Crispus's successor, or a second ruler
decisions.reason: Some synagogues had more than one ruler (13:15). Paul writes 1 Corinthians with "Sosthenes our brother" (1 Corinthians 1:1). It is not known whether that is the same man.

decisions.choice: none of these things mattered to Gallio: he did not step in
alternatives: he did not know about it
decisions.reason: Gallio let the beating happen in front of his own judgment seat. He had already said these matters were not his concern (18:15).

decisions.choice: in front of the court
decisions.reason: As in 18:16, Readable uses a familiar word.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔτι προσμείνας ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀποταξάμενος ἐξέπλει εἰς τὴν Συρίαν, καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας, κειράμενος ἐν Κεγχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν, εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν.

records.literal_gloss: The now Paul yet having remained days many, to the brothers having taken leave, sailed away to the Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having shaved in Cenchreae the head, he had for a vow.

en.L: And Paul, having stayed on many days more, took leave of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and sailed away to Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having shaved [his] head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
en.B: Paul remained many days longer. Then he took leave of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and sailed for Syria, and Priscilla and Aquila went with him. In Cenchreae he had his head shaved, since he had made a vow.
en.R: Paul stayed in Corinth for many more days. Then he said goodbye to the believers and got on a ship to go to Syria. Priscilla and Aquila went with him. At the port of Cenchreae he had his hair cut off, because he had made a special promise to God.

es.L: Y Pablo, habiéndose quedado aún muchos días, se despidió de los hermanos y navegó hacia Siria, y con él Priscila y Aquila, habiéndose rapado la cabeza en Cencreas, porque tenía un voto.
es.B: Pablo se quedó todavía muchos días más. Luego se despidió de los hermanos y se embarcó rumbo a Siria, y Priscila y Aquila fueron con él. En Cencreas se hizo rapar la cabeza, porque había hecho un voto.
es.R: Pablo se quedó en Corinto muchos días más. Después se despidió de los creyentes y subió a un barco para ir a Siria. Priscila y Aquila fueron con él. En el puerto de Cencreas se hizo cortar todo el pelo, porque le había hecho una promesa especial a Dios.

fr.L: Et Paul, étant resté encore bien des jours, prit congé des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et s’embarqua pour la Syrie, et avec lui Priscille et Aquilas, s’étant fait tondre la tête à Cenchrées, car il avait un vœu.
fr.B: Paul resta encore bien des jours. Puis il prit congé des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et s’embarqua pour la Syrie, accompagné de Priscille et d’Aquilas. À Cenchrées, il se fit raser la tête, car il avait fait un vœu.
fr.R: Paul est resté à Corinthe encore beaucoup de jours. Ensuite, il a dit au revoir aux croyants et il est monté sur un bateau pour aller en Syrie. Priscille et Aquilas sont partis avec lui. Au port de Cenchrées, il s’est fait couper les cheveux, parce qu’il avait fait une promesse spéciale à Dieu.

sw.L: Na Paulo, akiisha kukaa [huko] siku nyingi zaidi, aliagana na ndugu akasafiri baharini kwenda Siria, na pamoja naye Prisila na Akila, akiwa amenyoa kichwa [chake] huko Kenkrea, kwa maana alikuwa na nadhiri.
sw.B: Paulo alikaa huko siku nyingi zaidi. Kisha akaagana na ndugu, akasafiri kwa meli kwenda Siria, na Prisila na Akila wakaenda pamoja naye. Huko Kenkrea alinyoa kichwa chake, kwa sababu alikuwa ameweka nadhiri.
sw.R: Paulo alikaa Korintho siku nyingi zaidi. Kisha akawaaga waumini, akapanda meli kwenda Siria. Prisila na Akila walikwenda pamoja naye. Katika bandari ya Kenkrea alinyoa nywele zake, kwa sababu alikuwa ametoa ahadi maalum kwa Mungu.

decisions.choice: he who shaved his head: probably Paul, possibly Aquila
decisions.reason: The words "having shaved" stand right after Aquila's name, and the form fits either man. But Paul is the subject of the whole sentence, and the story follows him. Later Paul joins men under a vow in Jerusalem (21:23-26).

decisions.choice: a vow: a promise to God, marked by cutting the hair
alternatives: a Nazirite vow ending at the temple, for certain
decisions.reason: Under the Nazirite vow a person let the hair grow and shaved it at the end, at the temple in Jerusalem (Numbers 6:1-21). Shaving the head here, far from the temple, may mark the end of a private vow, or the start of a vow to be completed in Jerusalem. Luke does not say what the vow was for.

decisions.choice: Cenchreae: the eastern port of Corinth
alternatives: a town on the way to Syria
decisions.reason: Cenchreae lay about seven miles east of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf, where ships sailed for Asia and the east. Phoebe served the church there (Romans 16:1).

decisions.choice: Syria: the Roman province, which included Antioch
decisions.reason: Paul's home church was at Antioch in Syria (13:1-3, 14:26). He lands at Caesarea first and comes to Antioch in 18:22.

decisions.choice: Priscilla named before Aquila
decisions.reason: Luke names her first here and in 18:26, as Paul does in Romans 16:3 and 2 Timothy 4:19. This may show that she was the more prominent of the two in the church, but neither writer says why.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means the fellow believers in Corinth, men and women.

decisions.choice: the believers; a special promise to God
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the believers and for a vow.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English has the gender setting, Spanish "hermanos" already includes the sisters, so it stays plain; the same in verse 27. Readable says "creyentes", as the English says "believers".

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the believers (L, B); "croyants" (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the fellow believers in Corinth, men and women, with the traditional "frères" as the alternative; Readable's "croyants" is already inclusive. The same in 18:27.

decisions.choice: ndugu (L, B); waumini (R), with no gender span
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already includes sisters, so the English gender span has no Swahili counterpart; the same in 18:27.

decisions.choice: nadhiri (L, B); ahadi maalum kwa Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: A promise made to God (meaning decision): "nadhiri" is the word for a vow to God; "kiapo" is an oath. Readable explains it as the English Readable does.

source.text: κατήντησαν δὲ εἰς Ἔφεσον, κἀκείνους κατέλιπεν αὐτοῦ, αὐτὸς δὲ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν διελέξατο τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις.

records.literal_gloss: They came now to Ephesus, and those he left there, he himself then having entered into the synagogue reasoned with the Jews.

en.L: And they came to Ephesus, and he left those [two] there, but he himself, having entered into the synagogue, reasoned with the Jews.
en.B: They arrived at Ephesus, where Paul was to leave Priscilla and Aquila. He went into the synagogue on his own and debated with the Jews.
en.R: They arrived in the city of Ephesus. Paul left Priscilla and Aquila there. But first Paul went into the synagogue by himself and talked with the Jews about his message.

es.L: Y llegaron a Éfeso, y dejó allí a aquellos [dos], pero él, entrando en la sinagoga, discutió con los judíos.
es.B: Llegaron a Éfeso, donde Pablo iba a dejar a Priscila y a Aquila. Él entró solo en la sinagoga y debatió con los judíos.
es.R: Llegaron a la ciudad de Éfeso. Pablo dejó allí a Priscila y a Aquila. Pero primero Pablo entró solo en la sinagoga y habló con los judíos acerca de su mensaje.

fr.L: Et ils arrivèrent à Éphèse, et il laissa là ceux-ci ; mais lui-même, étant entré dans la synagogue, discuta avec les Juifs.
fr.B: Ils arrivèrent à Éphèse, où Paul devait laisser Priscille et Aquilas. Il entra seul dans la synagogue et discuta avec les Juifs.
fr.R: Ils sont arrivés dans la ville d’Éphèse. Paul y a laissé Priscille et Aquilas. Mais d’abord, Paul est allé seul à la synagogue et il a parlé de son message avec les Juifs.

sw.L: Na walifika Efeso, naye akawaacha hao huko, lakini yeye mwenyewe, akiisha kuingia katika sinagogi, alihojiana na Wayahudi.
sw.B: Walifika Efeso, ambako Paulo angewaacha Prisila na Akila. Yeye mwenyewe aliingia katika sinagogi, akajadiliana na Wayahudi.
sw.R: Walifika katika mji wa Efeso. Paulo aliwaacha Prisila na Akila huko. Lakini kwanza Paulo aliingia katika sinagogi peke yake, akazungumza na Wayahudi kuhusu ujumbe wake.

decisions.choice: Ephesus: the great port city of the province of Asia
decisions.reason: Ephesus lay on the west coast of what is now Turkey, across the Aegean Sea from Corinth. Paul later spends more than two years there (19:8-10).

decisions.choice: he left them there: told first, though it happened after his visit to the synagogue
alternatives: he left them before going to the synagogue
decisions.reason: Luke finishes the couple's part of the story before telling what Paul did. Paul himself leaves Ephesus in 18:21, so his visit to the synagogue came before the parting.

decisions.choice: reasoned: discussed and argued, as in 18:4
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 17:2 and 18:4.

decisions.choice: Priscilla and Aquila
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two.

decisions.choice: But first; about his message
alternatives: no time word; reasoned with the Jews
decisions.reason: Readable puts the events in order, following the meaning note, and says what the discussion was about.

source.text: ἐρωτώντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον μεῖναι οὐκ ἐπένευσεν, ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ εἰπών· Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ θεοῦ θέλοντος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου, καὶ κατελθὼν εἰς Καισάρειαν, ἀναβὰς καὶ ἀσπασάμενος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατέβη εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, καὶ ποιήσας χρόνον τινὰ ἐξῆλθεν, διερχόμενος καθεξῆς τὴν Γαλατικὴν χώραν καὶ Φρυγίαν, στηρίζων πάντας τοὺς μαθητάς.

records.literal_gloss: Asking now of them for longer time to remain, not he consented, \v 21 but having taken leave and having said, Again I will return to you, the God willing, he sailed from the Ephesus, \v 22 and having come down to Caesarea, having gone up and having greeted the church, he went down to Antioch, \v 23 and having spent time some he went out, passing through in order the Galatian region and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

en.L: And when they asked [him] to stay for a longer time, he did not consent, \v 21 but taking leave [of them] and saying, "I will return to you again, God willing," he set sail from Ephesus. \v 22 And having landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church, [and] went down to Antioch. \v 23 And having spent some time [there], he went out, passing through the Galatian region and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
en.B: They urged him to stay longer, but he would not agree. \v 21 As he said goodbye, he told them, "I will come back to you, if God wills," and he put out to sea from Ephesus. \v 22 He came ashore at Caesarea, went up to greet the church, and then went down to Antioch. \v 23 After some time there he set out again and journeyed through the Galatian country and Phrygia, town after town, building up all the disciples.
en.R: The Jews there asked Paul to stay longer, but he said no. \v 21 As he was leaving, he told them, "If God wants me to, I will come back to you." Then he sailed away from Ephesus. \v 22 He landed at the city of Caesarea. Then he went up to Jerusalem and greeted the church there. After that he went down to the city of Antioch. \v 23 Paul stayed in Antioch for a while. Then he left and went through the areas of Galatia and Phrygia, visiting one town after another. He helped all the followers of Jesus there to grow stronger.

es.L: Y rogándole ellos que se quedara más tiempo, no accedió, \v 21 sino que, despidiéndose [de ellos] y diciendo: «Otra vez volveré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si Dios quiere», zarpó de Éfeso. \v 22 Y habiendo desembarcado en Cesarea, subió y saludó a la iglesia, [y] bajó a Antioquía. \v 23 Y habiendo pasado [allí] algún tiempo, salió, recorriendo por orden la región de Galacia y Frigia, fortaleciendo a todos los discípulos.
es.B: Ellos le pidieron que se quedara más tiempo, pero él no aceptó. \v 21 Al despedirse, les dijo: «Volveré a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}}, si Dios quiere», y zarpó de Éfeso. \v 22 Desembarcó en Cesarea, subió a saludar a la iglesia y luego bajó a Antioquía. \v 23 Después de pasar allí algún tiempo, partió de nuevo y recorrió la región de Galacia y Frigia, pueblo tras pueblo, fortaleciendo a todos los discípulos.
es.R: Los judíos de allí le pidieron a Pablo que se quedara más tiempo, pero él dijo que no. \v 21 Al irse, les dijo: «Si Dios quiere, volveré a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}}». Luego se fue de Éfeso en barco. \v 22 Llegó a la ciudad de Cesarea. Después subió a Jerusalén y saludó a la iglesia de allí. Luego bajó a la ciudad de Antioquía. \v 23 Pablo se quedó un tiempo en Antioquía. Después se fue y recorrió las regiones de Galacia y Frigia, visitando un pueblo tras otro. Ayudó a todos los discípulos de esos lugares a hacerse más fuertes.

fr.L: Et comme ils [lui] demandaient de rester plus longtemps, il n’y consentit pas, \v 21 mais, prenant congé [d’eux] et disant : « Je reviendrai encore vers vous, si Dieu le veut », il partit d’Éphèse par mer. \v 22 Et, étant descendu à Césarée, il monta saluer l’église, [puis] descendit à Antioche. \v 23 Et, ayant passé quelque temps [là], il partit, parcourant successivement la région galatique et la Phrygie, affermissant tous les disciples.
fr.B: Ils le prièrent de rester plus longtemps, mais il refusa. \v 21 En leur faisant ses adieux, il leur dit : « Je reviendrai chez vous, si Dieu le veut. » Et il prit la mer depuis Éphèse. \v 22 Il débarqua à Césarée, monta saluer l’église, puis descendit à Antioche. \v 23 Après y avoir passé quelque temps, il repartit et parcourut, de ville en ville, la région galate et la Phrygie, affermissant tous les disciples.
fr.R: Les Juifs d’Éphèse ont demandé à Paul de rester plus longtemps, mais il a dit non. \v 21 Au moment de partir, il leur a dit : « Si Dieu le veut, je reviendrai vous voir. » Puis il est parti d’Éphèse en bateau. \v 22 Il a débarqué dans la ville de Césarée. Ensuite, il est monté à Jérusalem et il a salué l’église de cette ville. Après cela, il est descendu dans la ville d’Antioche. \v 23 Paul est resté quelque temps à Antioche. Puis il est reparti et il a traversé les régions de la Galatie et de la Phrygie, en allant d’une ville à l’autre. Il a aidé tous les disciples de Jésus de ces régions à devenir plus forts dans leur foi.

sw.L: Na walipomwomba akae muda mrefu zaidi, hakukubali, \v 21 bali akiisha kuagana nao na kusema, "Nitarudi kwenu tena, Mungu akipenda," aliondoka Efeso kwa meli. \v 22 Na akiisha kushuka Kaisaria, alipanda akalisalimu kanisa, [kisha] akashuka Antiokia. \v 23 Na akiisha kukaa [huko] muda fulani, aliondoka, akipita katika eneo la Galatia na Frigia mahali kwa mahali, akiwaimarisha wanafunzi wote.
sw.B: Walimsihi akae muda mrefu zaidi, lakini hakukubali. \v 21 Alipokuwa akiwaaga, aliwaambia, "Nitarudi kwenu, Mungu akipenda," kisha akaanza safari ya baharini kutoka Efeso. \v 22 Alishuka pwani huko Kaisaria, akapanda kulisalimu kanisa, kisha akashuka Antiokia. \v 23 Baada ya kukaa huko kwa muda, aliondoka tena, akapita katika nchi ya Galatia na Frigia mji kwa mji, akiwaimarisha wanafunzi wote.
sw.R: Wayahudi wa huko walimwomba Paulo akae muda mrefu zaidi, lakini alikataa. \v 21 Alipokuwa akiondoka, aliwaambia, "Mungu akipenda, nitarudi kwenu." Kisha akasafiri kwa meli kutoka Efeso. \v 22 Alishuka katika mji wa Kaisaria. Kisha akapanda kwenda Yerusalemu, akalisalimu kanisa la huko. Baada ya hapo akashuka mpaka mji wa Antiokia. \v 23 Paulo alikaa Antiokia kwa muda. Kisha akaondoka, akapita katika maeneo ya Galatia na Frigia, akitembelea mji mmoja baada ya mwingine. Aliwasaidia wanafunzi wote wa huko wawe imara zaidi.

decisions.choice: they: the Jews of the synagogue in Ephesus
decisions.reason: The last people named are the Jews Paul spoke with (18:19). Their request shows that they were open to hearing more.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: no words about a feast
alternatives: many manuscripts add that he must keep the coming feast in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add that Paul said he must by all means keep the coming feast in Jerusalem. The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God willing: if God allows it
decisions.reason: Paul leaves his plans to God (1 Corinthians 4:19, 16:7; James 4:15). He did come back (19:1).

decisions.choice: he went up and greeted the church: he went up to Jerusalem
alternatives: he greeted the church in Caesarea
decisions.reason: "Going up" is the usual way of speaking of travel to Jerusalem, which stands high in the hills (11:2, 15:2, 21:12). From there one "went down" to Antioch. Luke does not name Jerusalem, so the church could be the one at Caesarea.

decisions.choice: the Galatian region and Phrygia: inland Asia Minor, where Paul had founded churches
alternatives: Galatia far to the north only
decisions.reason: Paul had visited churches in this area before (14:21-23, 16:1-6). Luke names the same areas in the other order in 16:6.

decisions.choice: strengthening: making the believers firm in their faith
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 14:22 and 15:41, where Paul strengthens the churches and urges them to remain in the faith.

decisions.choice: put out to sea
decisions.reason: The verb is a sailing term for setting out from port.

decisions.choice: The Jews there; went up to Jerusalem; stayed in Antioch
alternatives: they; having gone up; having spent some time
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and places, following the meaning notes. Jerusalem is the probable reading, not a certain one.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable uses the same plain phrase as in 6:1-2.

decisions.choice: discípulos
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers of Jesus", Spanish keeps "discípulos" at every level, as across the Spanish New Testament; the word is plain in Spanish. The same in verse 27.

decisions.choice: l’église, lowercase
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles: one congregation, here probably the church in Jerusalem (m4), takes the lowercase; the capital is kept for the whole body of believers.

decisions.choice: les disciples de Jésus (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers of Jesus"; French keeps the key term "disciples" at every level and adds "de Jésus", which makes it just as clear. The same in 18:27.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi (R)
decisions.reason: "Wanafunzi" at every level, as the project's Swahili term list settles, where the English Readable says "followers of Jesus"; the same in 18:27.

source.text: Ἰουδαῖος δέ τις Ἀπολλῶς ὀνόματι, Ἀλεξανδρεὺς τῷ γένει, ἀνὴρ λόγιος, κατήντησεν εἰς Ἔφεσον, δυνατὸς ὢν ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς.

records.literal_gloss: A Jew now certain Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by the birth, a man eloquent, came to Ephesus, mighty being in the Scriptures.

en.L: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus, being mighty in the Scriptures.
en.B: A Jew called Apollos, born in Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was a gifted speaker and could handle the Scriptures with power.
en.R: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. He was from the city of Alexandria in Egypt. He was a very good speaker, and he knew the Scriptures very well.

es.L: Y cierto judío llamado Apolos, alejandrino de nacimiento, hombre elocuente, llegó a Éfeso, siendo poderoso en las Escrituras.
es.B: Llegó a Éfeso un judío llamado Apolos, nacido en Alejandría. Era un orador dotado y manejaba las Escrituras con poder.
es.R: Un judío llamado Apolos llegó a Éfeso. Era de la ciudad de Alejandría, en Egipto. Hablaba muy bien y conocía muy bien las Escrituras.

fr.L: Or un Juif nommé Apollos, Alexandrin de naissance, homme éloquent, arriva à Éphèse ; il était puissant dans les Écritures.
fr.B: Un Juif nommé Apollos, originaire d’Alexandrie, arriva à Éphèse. C’était un orateur de talent, qui maniait les Écritures avec puissance.
fr.R: Un Juif appelé Apollos est arrivé à Éphèse. Il venait de la ville d’Alexandrie, en Égypte. C’était un très bon orateur, et il connaissait très bien les Écritures.

sw.L: Basi Myahudi mmoja jina lake Apolo, mzaliwa wa Aleksandria, mtu mwenye ufasaha, alifika Efeso, akiwa hodari katika Maandiko.
sw.B: Myahudi mmoja aitwaye Apolo, mzaliwa wa Aleksandria, alifika Efeso. Alikuwa msemaji hodari, na aliweza kuyatumia Maandiko kwa nguvu.
sw.R: Myahudi mmoja aitwaye Apolo alifika Efeso. Alitoka mji wa Aleksandria huko Misri. Alikuwa msemaji mzuri sana, naye aliyajua Maandiko vizuri sana.

decisions.choice: Alexandria: the great city of Egypt, with a large Jewish community
decisions.reason: Alexandria was a leading center of Greek learning. Many Jews lived there, and the Jewish thinker Philo wrote there in the first century. Jews from Alexandria had their own synagogue in Jerusalem (6:9).

decisions.choice: eloquent: skilled with words, perhaps also learned
decisions.reason: The word can mean a skilled speaker or a man of learning. "Mighty in the Scriptures" already speaks of his learning, so the stress may be on his speaking. Later some in Corinth preferred him to Paul (1 Corinthians 1:12, 3:4-6).

decisions.choice: mighty in the Scriptures: able to explain and argue from the Scriptures
decisions.reason: "Mighty" here means able. 18:28 shows how he used the Scriptures. The Scriptures are what Christians now call the Old Testament.

decisions.choice: the city of Alexandria in Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says where Alexandria was.

source.text: οὗτος ἦν κατηχημένος τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι ἐλάλει καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ἀκριβῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐπιστάμενος μόνον τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου.

records.literal_gloss: This [man] was having been instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in the spirit he was speaking and was teaching accurately the things concerning the Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John.

en.L: This [man] had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in spirit, he was speaking and teaching accurately the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John.
en.B: He had been taught the way of the Lord, and with great zeal he spoke and taught the facts about Jesus correctly, though the only baptism he knew was John's.
en.R: Someone had taught him about the way of the Lord. He was full of excitement when he spoke and taught, and what he taught about Jesus was correct. But the only baptism he knew about was the one John had preached.

es.L: Este había sido instruido en el camino del Señor, y siendo ferviente de espíritu, hablaba y enseñaba con exactitud las cosas acerca de Jesús, conociendo solo el bautismo de Juan.
es.B: Había sido instruido en el camino del Señor, y con gran fervor hablaba y enseñaba con exactitud lo referente a Jesús, aunque solo conocía el bautismo de Juan.
es.R: Alguien le había enseñado acerca del camino del Señor. Hablaba y enseñaba con mucho entusiasmo, y lo que enseñaba acerca de Jesús era correcto. Pero el único bautismo que conocía era el que Juan había predicado.

fr.L: Celui-ci avait été instruit dans la voie du Seigneur et, fervent d’esprit, il parlait et enseignait avec exactitude ce qui concernait Jésus, ne connaissant que le baptême de Jean.
fr.B: On lui avait enseigné la voie du Seigneur et, plein de zèle, il parlait et enseignait correctement ce qui concernait Jésus, mais il ne connaissait que le baptême de Jean.
fr.R: Quelqu’un lui avait appris la voie du Seigneur. Il parlait et il enseignait avec beaucoup d’enthousiasme, et ce qu’il enseignait sur Jésus était juste. Mais le seul baptême qu’il connaissait, c’était celui que Jean avait prêché.

sw.L: Huyu alikuwa amefundishwa njia ya Bwana, na akiwa na bidii katika roho, alikuwa akinena na kufundisha kwa usahihi mambo yanayomhusu Yesu, akijua ubatizo wa Yohana tu.
